takeaway: IMN flips today’s Nicoya Peninsula into afternoon/evening showers and thunderstorms as trades ease and Pacific moisture rises, with heat near 36–37°C. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development interest stays well southwest of Mexico and farther west, not aimed at Nicoya.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu–Sat)
periods.pattern: Today: IMN Pacífico Norte — clearer mornings, then peninsula showers/storms afternoon–evening and some coastal rain overnight; muggy as alisios weaken. Fri–Sat: models keep typical wet-season cells; ECMWF 00Z is wetter into Sat (~1–2 in / 24 h over Nicoya on maps) while GFS/GEFS/EPS/EC-AIFS stay closer to light–moderate (roughly 0.1–0.75 in). Papagayo still fresh early (NHC).
periods.implications: Plan outdoor time for mornings; expect disruptive late-day storms today especially. Heat is the other limiter. Not a locked multi-day temporal yet.
periods.confidence: High for IMN’s Thu storm theme and no nearby TC. Moderate on Fri–Sat amounts (deterministic spread).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun–Wed)
periods.pattern: GFS 06Z shows a wetter Nicoya pulse around Sun (~0.75–1.25 in / 24 h ending 20 Sep 06Z) then lighter early next week, with a broader Caribbean/Pacific low and more SW 850 hPa flow by ~Wed 23 on that one run. GEFS mean and AIFS-ENS at similar range do not show a closed Central American gyre; ECMWF 00Z at Sun keeps Caribbean high / more easterly trades.
periods.implications: Treat weekend–early-week rain as on-and-off cells, not a guaranteed temporales. Flexibility still beats firm outdoor bookings late day.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances; low–moderate for a sustained Pacific-side temporales or gyre.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain. CPC GTH (valid 23 Sep–6 Oct, text updated 15 Sep) still favors below-average Caribbean rainfall weeks 2–3; EPAC genesis risk is coastal Mexico, not CR. GFS day-9ish maps still show only light–moderate Nicoya totals amid distant EPAC convection.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly Tue–Wed 22–23 Sep only if flanking lows and sustained Pacific SW low-level flow verify; not supported as a closed gyre in current ensemble means
gyreWatch.supporting: GFS 06Z 17 Sep ~f144 shows a broad Caribbean ~1004 hPa low east of Nicaragua/CR and more SW/W 850 hPa flow over Nicoya; IMN already notes easing trades and Pacific moisture today.
gyreWatch.conflicting: GEFS mean and AIFS-ENS ~f144–150 lack a closed Central American gyre; ECMWF/AIFS-ENS around Sun favor Caribbean high / weaker organization; NHC has no disturbance near CR; IMN sub-seasonal still Pacific deficit. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities.

whatChanged: Yesterday’s midweek “isolated peninsula showers” theme is outdated: IMN now explicitly targets Nicoya afternoon storms today. Weekend wetter risk remains, but ensembles are milder than ECMWF’s wetter Sat and GFS’s Sun pulse, and the late-week gyre idea is still only a GFS-leaning scenario, not ensemble-backed.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Thu–Sat before convective peaks; today is the day to finish plans early. Worth planning around: afternoon/evening thunderstorms and heat (IMN Nicoya max ~36.6°C), Papagayo NE–E 20–25 kt with seas ~6–8 ft today easing Fri onward (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113).
